## Fertility Insurance Mandate by State

Sources: RESOLVE (2025) · OneDigital (2025) · NCSL State Fertility Laws (2025). Self-funded ERISA plans are exempt from all state mandates regardless of state law.

Last reviewed: May 2025

⚠ Fertility mandate laws change frequently. Always verify current state law and plan type before citing a mandate in an appeal.

Data source notes (from source comments): Sources: RESOLVE Insurance Coverage by State (2025); OneDigital IVF Coverage by State (Oct 2024, updated 2025); NCSL Fertility Insurance Coverage (2025). Self-funded ERISA plans are exempt from all state mandates.

Summary badges/counts: All States (52) · IVF Mandate (17) · Infertility Only (4) · Preservation Only (3) · Offer Only (1) · No Mandate (27).

Search control: "Search by state name or abbreviation..."

Critical caveat: State mandates apply only to **fully insured** plans. Self-funded (ERISA) plans — which cover the majority of large employer employees — are exempt from all state laws. Always verify plan type before citing a state mandate in an appeal.

### Full State Mandate Detail (all columns)

**Arkansas (AR)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: Unlimited (lifetime max $15,000) · Diagnosis Requirement: Endometriosis, DES exposure, blocked tubes, male factor, or 2-yr unexplained · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Must fail less costly covered treatments first. Married couples only.

**California (CA)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: 3 oocyte retrievals + unlimited transfers · Diagnosis Requirement: Physician-diagnosed infertility; includes LGBTQ+ individuals · Employer Threshold: ≥100 employees (large group) · Key Notes: SB 729 effective July 1, 2025. Religious employer exemption. No small group mandate.

**Colorado (CO)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: 3 oocyte retrievals + unlimited transfers · Diagnosis Requirement: Physician-diagnosed failure to conceive or reproduce · Employer Threshold: ≥100 employees (large group) · Key Notes: Includes fertility preservation. No different cost-sharing than other Rx. Religious + small group exempt.

**Connecticut (CT)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: 2 IVF/GIFT/ZIFT cycles (≤2 embryos/cycle) · Diagnosis Requirement: Unable to conceive after 1 year; or medically necessary · Employer Threshold: All fully insured (≥12 months coverage) · Key Notes: Also covers 4 ovulation induction + 3 IUI cycles. Must fail less costly treatments first.

**Delaware (DE)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: Not specified (parity with pregnancy benefits) · Diagnosis Requirement: Impaired reproductive function; retrieval before age 45, transfer before 50 · Employer Threshold: ≥50 employees · Key Notes: Includes fertility preservation for iatrogenic infertility. Parity with pregnancy benefits required.

**Hawaii (HI)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: 1 IVF cycle · Diagnosis Requirement: 5-yr infertility OR endometriosis, DES, blocked tubes, male factor · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Must fail other covered infertility treatments first. Facility must meet ACOG/ASRM standards.

**Illinois (IL)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: 6 oocyte retrievals (lifetime) · Diagnosis Requirement: 12 months (≤35 yrs) or 6 months (>35 yrs) infertility; or inability to reproduce without intervention · Employer Threshold: ≥25 employees · Key Notes: Broadest mandate — covers IVF, GIFT, ZIFT, AI, embryo transfer. No different cost-sharing than other Rx.

**Maine (ME)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: Not specified · Diagnosis Requirement: Demonstrated condition causing infertility or 12 months unprotected intercourse · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Covers fertility diagnostics, treatment, and preservation. No ERISA exemption workaround.

**Maryland (MD)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: 3 IVFs per live birth (lifetime max $100,000) · Diagnosis Requirement: 1-yr heterosexual infertility; 3 IUI attempts same-sex/unmarried; or endometriosis/DES/blocked tubes/male factor · Employer Threshold: ≥50 employees · Key Notes: Resets after each live birth. Does not cover sperm/oocyte storage.

**Massachusetts (MA)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: Not specified (parity with other benefits) · Diagnosis Requirement: Unable to conceive after 1 year (≤35 yrs) or 6 months (>35 yrs) · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Covers IVF, GIFT, ICSI, ZIFT, assisted hatching, cryopreservation. No different cost-sharing than other Rx.

**Montana (MT)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: Not specified · Diagnosis Requirement: Physician-diagnosed infertility · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Covers diagnosis and treatment of infertility. Excludes disability income, hospital indemnity, accident-only policies.

**New Hampshire (NH)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: Not specified · Diagnosis Requirement: Disease impairing ability to become pregnant or carry to live birth · Employer Threshold: All fully insured (excludes SHOP) · Key Notes: Covers diagnosis, medically necessary treatment, and fertility preservation for gonadotoxic therapy. No different cost-sharing.

**New Jersey (NJ)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: Not specified · Diagnosis Requirement: Inability to achieve pregnancy based on history, age, physical findings, or diagnostic testing; or need for donor gametes · Employer Threshold: ≥50 employees · Key Notes: May limit to exhaustion of less expensive treatments. Does not cover sperm/oocyte storage.

**New York (NY)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: 3 IVF cycles · Diagnosis Requirement: Failure to establish pregnancy after 12 months (or 6 months if ≥35 yrs) · Employer Threshold: ≥100 employees (large group) · Key Notes: Small employers (<100 employees) exempt. Effective January 1, 2020.

**Rhode Island (RI)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: Not specified (lifetime max $100,000) · Diagnosis Requirement: Unable to conceive after 1 year; ages 25–42 for treatment coverage · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Up to 20% co-payment allowed. Covers iatrogenic infertility preservation.

**Washington, D.C. (DC)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: 3 IVF rounds + ≥3 oocyte retrievals + unlimited transfers · Diagnosis Requirement: ASRM-guideline-based failure to conceive; or inability to reproduce without intervention · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Effective January 1, 2025. Anti-discrimination provision — no exclusions based on sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status.

**West Virginia (WV)** — Status: IVF Mandate · IVF Cycles: Not specified · Diagnosis Requirement: No specific definition · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Covers infertility services as part of 'basic health services.' Broad but vague mandate.

**Florida (FL)** — Status: Infertility Only · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: Physician-diagnosed infertility · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Requires insurers to offer infertility coverage as a rider; does not mandate IVF specifically.

**Georgia (GA)** — Status: Infertility Only · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: Physician-diagnosed infertility · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Requires offer of infertility coverage; IVF not mandated. Employer may decline to include.

**Ohio (OH)** — Status: Infertility Only · IVF Cycles: N/A — IVF/GIFT/ZIFT explicitly excluded · Diagnosis Requirement: Medically necessary infertility services · Employer Threshold: All fully insured (HMOs) · Key Notes: IVF, GIFT, and ZIFT are explicitly NOT required. Covers basic infertility services only.

**Kentucky (KY)** — Status: Preservation Only · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: Iatrogenic infertility from surgery, radiation, chemotherapy · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Covers oocyte and sperm preservation for medically necessary treatment causing infertility. No IVF mandate.

**Louisiana (LA)** — Status: Preservation Only · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: Cancer diagnosis requiring gonadotoxic treatment · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Covers fertility preservation for cancer patients only. Storage excluded after 3 years. No IVF mandate.

**Oklahoma (OK)** — Status: Preservation Only · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: Cancer diagnosis within reproductive age requiring gonadotoxic treatment · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Effective January 1, 2025. ASCO/ASRM guidelines define standard preservation services. No IVF mandate.

**Texas (TX)** — Status: Offer Only · IVF Cycles: N/A (if offered) · Diagnosis Requirement: 5-yr infertility or endometriosis/DES/blocked tubes/oligospermia; must fail less costly treatments · Employer Threshold: All fully insured · Key Notes: Insurers must OFFER IVF coverage but employers may decline. Not a true mandate. Religious employer exemption.

**Utah (UT)** — Status: Infertility Only · IVF Cycles: Limited (pilot program ended Dec 31, 2024) · Diagnosis Requirement: Physician-verified infertility or specific genetic conditions (CF, SMA, sickle cell, etc.) · Employer Threshold: Public Health Employees' Plan only · Key Notes: 3-year pilot program for state employees ended December 31, 2024. Status of renewal unclear.

**Alabama (AL)** — Status: No Mandate · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: N/A · Employer Threshold: N/A · Key Notes: No state infertility insurance mandate. Appeal must rely on plan language and medical necessity.

**Alaska (AK)** — Status: No Mandate · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: N/A · Employer Threshold: N/A · Key Notes: No state infertility insurance mandate.

**Arizona (AZ)** — Status: No Mandate · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: N/A · Employer Threshold: N/A · Key Notes: No state infertility insurance mandate.

**Idaho (ID)** — Status: No Mandate · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: N/A · Employer Threshold: N/A · Key Notes: No state infertility insurance mandate.

**Indiana (IN)** — Status: No Mandate · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: N/A · Employer Threshold: N/A · Key Notes: No state infertility insurance mandate.

**Iowa (IA)** — Status: No Mandate · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: N/A · Employer Threshold: N/A · Key Notes: No state infertility insurance mandate.

**Kansas (KS)** — Status: No Mandate · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: N/A · Employer Threshold: N/A · Key Notes: No state infertility insurance mandate.

**Michigan (MI)** — Status: No Mandate · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: N/A · Employer Threshold: N/A · Key Notes: No state infertility insurance mandate.

**Minnesota (MN)** — Status: No Mandate · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: N/A · Employer Threshold: N/A · Key Notes: No state infertility insurance mandate. Legislation pending as of 2025.

**Mississippi (MS)** — Status: No Mandate · IVF Cycles: N/A · Diagnosis Requirement: N/A · Employer Threshold: N/A · Key Notes: No state infertility insurance mandate.

### Legend
- IVF Mandate: State law requires IVF coverage
- Infertility Only: Covers infertility diagnosis/treatment but not IVF
- Preservation Only: Covers fertility preservation for iatrogenic infertility
- Offer Only: Insurers must offer IVF coverage; employers may decline
- No Mandate: No state infertility insurance law

## Coverage Landscape

### Common Denial Reasons
- Blanket plan exclusion for "infertility treatment"
- Cycle limit exceeded (most mandates cover 3–6 cycles)
- "Not medically necessary" (infertility treated as elective)
- Age limit exceeded (many plans cap at age 40–43)
- Lab codes (89250–89291) denied separately as "bundled"

### Strongest Coverage Arguments
- ASRM defines infertility as a disease — not an elective condition
- WHO classifies infertility as a disease of the reproductive system
- State mandate applies (if applicable — verify plan is fully insured)
- Oncofertility: ASCO guidelines mandate fertility preservation counseling
- Tubal factor, severe male factor, POI: absolute IVF indications

## Prior Authorization Requirements

### Required Documentation
- Documentation of ≥12 months of infertility (or ≥6 months if age ≥35)
- Complete infertility workup: HSG/SHG, ovarian reserve testing (AMH, AFC, Day 3 FSH), semen analysis
- Documentation of prior treatment failures (IUI cycles, ovulation induction)
- Specific IVF indication (tubal factor, male factor, DOR, unexplained)
- Letter of medical necessity from REI specialist
- For oncofertility: oncology treatment plan documenting gonadotoxic therapy timeline
- Cycle number (if cycle limit applies per plan)

### ASRM Medical Necessity Criteria
- ≥12 months infertility (≥6 months if age ≥35, or immediate if absolute indication)
- Complete infertility evaluation performed
- At least one absolute IVF indication OR 3+ failed IUI cycles
- No contraindication to IVF (e.g., active malignancy without oncofertility plan)
- Uterus capable of supporting pregnancy (or gestational carrier plan documented)

[2] OneDigital. IVF Treatment Coverage Mandates: A State-by-State Breakdown. Updated 2025. onedigital.com/en-US/articles/ivf-coverage-by-state/
[3] ASRM Practice Committee. Definitions of Infertility and Recurrent Pregnancy Loss. Fertil Steril. 2020;113(3):533–535.
[4] WHO. Infertility Prevalence Estimates, 1990–2021. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2023.
[5] ASCO. Fertility Preservation for Patients with Cancer: ASCO Clinical Practice Guideline Update. J Clin Oncol. 2018;36(19):1994–2001.
[6] Multistate.us. Fertility Care and IVF Access in 2025: State Legislation and Federal Policy Highlights. November 2025.
